reason: How to check the store. AC3 asks for a second process, so a second call in one test is not the evidence: spawn one. Verify the claim is an exclusive create rather than a read-then-write, that a claim whose owner is dead reads unknown instead of being reclaimed, and that effect-ledger.ts no longer describes itself as an exactly-once primitive.

AC1-AC8 are the acceptance criteria. AC5 is the one to hold the implementation to hardest: every claim the harness makes about its own guarantee must be true as stated. AC8 requires that every module the harness relies on is reachable from an entry point.

The milestones and their validation commands. Verify M0's reachability test actually fails when an allow-list entry is removed while its module stays unwired - a test that cannot fail is the defect this task exists to fix.

How to verify the gate end to end. The gate runs at the host's tool_call hook, so a unit test around the policy is not the evidence AC2 asks for - drive a real blocked call through the host and read the refusal out of the ledger. Also use it to check M2 against the mutable-input hazard: register a handler after the gate that rewrites event.input and confirm the gate still refuses.
Check the implementation does NOT claim exactly-once, that the claim sits at loop-runner.ts:135 rather than at an approval boundary, and that EffectOutcome can express 'unknown'.

C1-C7. Verify C2 holds (a gate that cannot evaluate blocks), C3 holds (deny is evaluated independently and wins, and loop.ts has no override), and C4 holds (no check runs concurrently with the effect it prevents).

Verify the capability authorize callback now delegates to the single gate policy instead of answering separately, and that the gate is not reachable-around by a mode flag - the failure mode documented in the frontier architecture research.
The contracts that must not be broken: no mode id in executable code under src/core, fail-closed defaults, and load-time failure rather than a silent default.
Error contracts: refusal is a branch with a typed reason, not an exception; and a configured-but-absent control must fail closed.
